title: Israel votes today: who is ahead?
lines: Israel is voting today, in its first election since the war with Iran began.
About seven point three million people are eligible to vote, including around one point two million Palestinian citizens of Israel.
There are more than twelve thousand polling stations, open from seven in the morning to ten at night, Israel time.
Thirty-seven parties are running, but a party needs at least three point two five percent of the vote to enter the Knesset.
In the final polls, former army chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party was narrowly ahead, with twenty-two to twenty-three seats.
Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud was projected at nineteen to twenty-one.
Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc was projected at about fifty seats, and the opposition at fifty-two to fifty-six. Neither reaches the sixty-one needed.
That means Palestinian-led parties, projected at fourteen to sixteen seats, could hold the balance.
President Isaac Herzog, voting in Jerusalem, said no one can be allowed to spoil or undermine the election.
Exit polls come at ten at night Israel time, which is one in the morning in Pakistan. Official results are due by the fourth of November.
And winning the most seats does not automatically decide who becomes prime minister. Coalition talks could take weeks.
